title: Shape the shell and test-page template
question: Three structures for where bench status, live outputs, hazard keys and the verdict live. The palette stays Anodized; this choice is composition. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Annunciator top bar
options.thesis: The top bar becomes the bench's annunciator: every output has a fixed window that lights, never one that appears.
options.viewport: 64px top bar: DUT and Instruments windows left of the centred search, RF / DC / LTE / RUN windows right of it, unlit ones dim. DUT row gone from pages (its controls open from the DUT window). Page header pairs the title with hazard-keyed Send/Run; Results lead with a verdict strip.
options.risk: The top bar gets busy at 1280 px; the windows must shed detail text, not positions, when narrow.

options.label: Preflight course
options.thesis: Every test page is a numbered course of checks that punch off as they pass, ending in Run and the verdict.
options.viewport: Under the page title a step rail: ① DUT ✓ ② Instruments 3/3 ✓ ③ Path loss ⚠ ④ Settings ⑤ Run. Finished steps fold to one line, the blocking step stays open, Run says what blocks it. Live outputs stay in the top bar as larger windows.
options.risk: Heavy for one-shot Manual pages; status lives per page, so it is not one consistent place across Components pages.

options.label: Run transport bar
options.thesis: One docked bar at the foot of every page holds the hazard keys, the run's progress and the verdict, where the eye returns from across the bench.
options.viewport: Bottom bar: DUT + Instruments lamps left; Stop, Run · TX and a labelled E-STOP centre over a progress track where every measured point lands as a tick (✕ for FAIL); ✓ PASS / ✕ FAIL tally and live outputs right. Pages above keep config and results; the header carries only quiet actions.
options.risk: Moves Send/Run away from the header operators know; the bar costs 76px of height on every page.
